newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Islamist group opposes Western democracy.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Islamist group opposes Western democracy.

text.p: A Kuwaiti Islamist political grouping has said it wants the Moslem Gulf state to abandon what it called Western-style democracy in favour of an Islamic Shura (consultative) system, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.
"The members of the so-called Shura Advocates Group called for replacing the democratic system that separates religion from the state with a Shura system," al-Seyssah newspaper reported.
Kuwait is the only Gulf Arab state with a fully elected parliament. The 62-member house has some 14 Islamist and pro-Islamist deputies.
"Kuwait's constitution combines...the pillars of the Islamic society and those of the civic Western democratic society," it quoted a statement by the grouping as saying.
"Democracy applies man-made laws while Islam requires that sharia (Islamic law) should be implemented," Ahmad Abdul-Aziz al-Muzaini, a member of the grouping, said.
The system envisaged by the grouping, which calls for boycotting parliamentary elections, would have a Shura council chosen by popular societies, tribal chiefs and clerics.
